methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $75M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Sofar Ocean is a Series B ocean and maritime technology company founded by Tim Janssen and Evan Shapiro, having raised $75M+ to date. The valuation analysis operates without direct public comparables or identified private peer transactions in the ocean and maritime technology sector, limiting triangulation to stage-based progression modeling.

The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $75M total capital raised, treating this as a proxy for current enterprise value. This methodology reflects typical step-up multiples observed in Series B to subsequent-stage financing rounds and yields an implied valuation of $142M. The analysis generates a range bounded by conservative ($121M, applying 1.6x) and optimistic ($164M, applying 2.2x) variants of this multiplier, reflecting normal variance in step-up ratios across comparable stage transitions.

The triangulation supports a median valuation of $142M with a plausible range of $121M to $164M. This range should be treated with material uncertainty given the single-method basis and absence of sector comparables. Key valuation drivers—market adoption of ocean monitoring technology, competitive positioning, revenue trajectory, and capital efficiency—cannot be quantified from available data. Investors should seek direct access to financial metrics, customer concentration, and technology differentiation before committing capital at any point within this range.
